newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Red flags, bunting for Kazakh capital's May Day.
newsitem.headline: Red flags, bunting for Kazakh capital's May Day.

text.p: Several hundred elderly demonstrators, nostalgic for the Soviet past, gathered in a park amid red flags and bunting in the Kazakh capital Almaty on May Day to protest against unpaid pensions and wages.
One banner trumpeted the traditional Soviet call "Proletarians of all countries -- unite!" while another, less orthodox placard declared: "Capitalism is shit."
Bunches of red carnations were placed at the foot of a statue of Bolshevik leader Vladimir Lenin, which was quietly removed by the authorities from the city centre last year.
The Workers' Movement, a Kazakh opposition group, organised the sanctioned demonstration.

One of its members read out over a loudspeaker parts of an open letter addressed to Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev: "The people are indignant at being robbed of the people's wealth under the slogan of privatisation."
Kazakhstan, an ex-Soviet state spread across an area of Central Asian steppe five times the size of France, is undergoing painful market economic reforms.

The government speaks of an imminent boom in the oil-rich republic but the reforms have so far passed by many of the 16.9 million population, many of whom have not received meagre salaries or pensions for months.
Many elderly people, who miss the certainties of their Soviet past, have to root in rubbish bins for food.

"Around the president are people who steal everything. The factories are closed, the factories aren't working," complained Nikolai Bashliev, a pensioner in his sixties. "The government is destroying pensioners.
